title: Portland

pages.message: Though small particles typically remain in the atmosphere for only a few days, they can be transported far away from source regions by large scale weather systems.

note: Ours: smog blown over the city and swept out again, picked by the app's rules and how fast its fog flows (section 5); every hour of it.

sources.source: GEOS-CF v1 (NASA GMAO), xgc_tavg_1hr_g1440x721_x1, the sum of aod550_bc, aod550_oc, aod550_sulfate, aod550_dust, aod550_sala, aod550_salc
sources.license: NASA data, no restrictions on use
sources.credit: Keller, C. A., et al. (2021). Description of the NASA GEOS composition forecast modeling system GEOS-CF v1.0. JAMES 13, e2020MS002413.
sources.substitute: EIC 5151 shows surface PM2.5 from GEOS-CF v2 (from 2025-08-04); the album plays the same model's column AOD (v1 holds every song), as surface PM2.5 empties and refills in place each day.

units.<lat>_<lon>: aerosol optical depth at 550 nm, unitless (hourly mean, the cell centred there)
